title: Boolean-lattice (zeta) finite networks: compiler-level construction, in-tree assembly projection 15x-48x, obligations named (research record, draft)
body:
**Research record (draft).** Adds `research/zeta-family/` only; no existing files change.

## Change and mathematical scope

A new finite-network construction, the **zeta family**, on the Boolean lattice. Inputs are all nonzero, non-full bitmasks of `[h]`; the DAG is the **fast Yates zeta transform**; the side root for target `t` is `Z_{full^t}` = the sum of every input submasked into `complement(t)`, i.e. bit-disjoint from `t`. The in-tree side-root orthogonality contract (value span inside the orthogonal complement of the targets' addresses) holds **by construction**. No center roots, so `ell = 0` and the in-tree identity gives `deficit = 2v`. The binding quantity is the role density `R/v`.

Compiled through the merged in-tree compiler (`scripts/paired_cube/frames.py::compile_graph`, the #144 path), priced through the in-tree assembly with both sides configured at the family saving (the two-sided projection):

| h | v | R | R/v | saving | kappa | x PR #163 (reference) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 6 | 12 | 2.00 | 3.0519e-2 | 2.8764e-2 | 48.4x |
| 4 | 14 | 38 | 2.71 | 1.7960e-2 | 1.7337e-2 | 29.2x |
| 5 | 30 | 100 | 3.33 | 1.2279e-2 | 1.1985e-2 | 20.2x |
| 6 | 62 | 242 | 3.90 | 9.0809e-3 | 8.9189e-3 | 15.0x |
| 7 | 126 | 560 | 4.44 | 7.0573e-3 | 6.9591e-3 | 11.7x |
| 8 | 254 | 1262 | 4.97 | 5.6780e-3 | 5.6142e-3 | 9.5x |

**Changed hypotheses:** none to the retained interfaces. `upstream/` untouched; no certificates, patches or `scripts/` edited.

**Open obligations (stated; this is not a reviewed headword claim).**
A. Source histogram shape supplied explicitly for `h <= 6` (the in-tree default `Counter({2:v, h-4:v, 1:v})` is a dict literal whose duplicate keys collapse at `h in {5,6}` and is negative at `h=3`; the supplied `{2:v, 1:v(h-3)}` is the legal mass-`v(h-1)` form and is conservative). `h >= 7` uses the default unchanged.
B. Centerless scope: `ell = 0` passes every in-tree assert; the role coordinate-star centers discharge in the retained notes is not re-derived.
C. **Semantics:** the DAG computes `y_t = sum_{u&t=0} x_u` (checked literally below). Its service to the upstream reduction - the analogue of `H+K+B = I` - is not established here and is the main open obligation.
D. The scalar word/replay **is included**: adjoint pre-reads on raw dirt, V-gates, compute, reads, full inverse; dirty scratch restored; four tamper controls rejected (mod 2^61-1 and integers; three seeds). Not built here: the physical placement/recycling layer. The graph verifies through the merged complex-side compiler path; the **bit-side path carries its own H0 = (I-J/9)/2 cap geometry and does not accept this graph as-is** (checked: rejects with 'root physical compatibility'), so the bit-side construction remains an obligation and every table number is a two-sided projection under A-C.

## Validation

`python3 research/zeta-family/verify.py` (stdlib only, run without `-O`, about 1 second):

- **Finite identity check (not a proof):** a literal semantic evaluation of the DAG - every root equals `sum_{u: u&t=0} x_u` for random inputs, both seeds, `h = 3..8`.
- The scalar word/replay: dirty scratch on every register, restored by the inverse pass; the map `y_t = sum_{u&t=0} x_u` recovered exactly; four tamper controls rejected, on two rings and three seeds, `h = 3..8`.
- The in-tree compiler's full assert chain on each graph, including `mass == h*R + ell` and `deficit == 2v - 3*ell`.
- The in-tree 47-constraint assembly with both sides at the family saving (`b < 1/32`, `b > a`, all 47 slacks, seven margins).
- `make paired-cube-verify`: PASS (recorded; the change adds files only, so the selected incremental target is unaffected).
- CI: `.github/workflows/zeta-family.yml` runs the package verifier on Python 3.11 and 3.13.

The frontier multiple is re-derived from PR #163's certified number and is a reference only.

## Credits

The compiler (`scripts/paired_cube/frames.py`), the assembly, the side-root orthogonality contract and the identity bookkeeping are icekylinx's #144 lineage, used unchanged. Graph construction, semantic evaluation and the audit table by this contribution, prepared with AI assistance (Cline). Apache-2.0.
